comparison: Perfect agreement on core finding (C1, C8-C11, C50). Both evaluations find strong support for enhanced neural responses to local prediction violations with statistical backing from calcium imaging data. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate this as SUPPORTED with high confidence.

Both address VIP interneuron responses to sequence termination (C3, C34-C42, C57-C58, C95). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while acknowledging functional interpretation as speculative. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting variability and difficulty interpreting VIP responses, requiring replication. Agreement on observations but divergence on confidence level.

Both address dissociation of adaptation from surprise mechanisms (C2, C17-C19, C23, C27-C33, C94). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with note about partial independence. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming the disentanglement of adaptation, surprise, and surprise adaptation. Strong agreement on this key finding.

Both address PV responses to global violations (C5-C6, C43-C48, C96). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite acknowledging weak effects. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, noting the value of cell-type-specific recordings while suggesting replication may be needed. Agreement on basic observations with shared acknowledgment of limitations.

Both address functional interpretation of VIP responses as chunking signals (C4, C59-C62). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of causal manipulation. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, noting variability and speculative nature of mechanistic interpretation. Strong agreement on uncertainty of functional claims.

Both address synthesis of dissociable mechanisms across experiments (C7, C55, C78, C82, C92, C97). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on comprehensive dataset. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, affirming this advances understanding of distinct predictive processes. Strong agreement on this integrative conclusion.

Both address cumulative violation effects in same neurons (C14, C56, C79, C93). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on clustering analysis. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, noting large dataset and compelling conclusions. Strong agreement on this finding.

Partial overlap on adaptation recovery time and inter-tone interval manipulation (C16, C20-C21, C52). OpenEval focuses on oddball paradigm controls. Peer review R3 addresses broader adaptation dissociation including these elements. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on sequence-structure-based predictions (C22, C24). OpenEval addresses contextual requirement for B tones. Peer review R3 includes these claims in broader discussion of adaptation dissociation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on conceptual definitions and summary statements (C25-C26, C49, C51, C53). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED as framework claims. Peer review R9 addresses broader summary conclusions including some overlapping claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address speculative explanations for weak global violation findings (C63, C65, C70, C74-C75). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting hypotheses not directly tested. Peer review R2 also rates as UNCERTAIN, noting qualitative differences between recording methods and need for detailed consideration. Agreement on uncertainty.

Partial overlap on species differences in global violation responses (C69, C71-C73). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for descriptive claims about current findings and prior literature. Peer review R2 addresses related concerns about interpretation (C69, C73, C74-C75) with UNCERTAIN rating. Divergence reflects different scope of claims being evaluated.

Partial overlap on theoretical implications and synthesis (C76-C77, C80-C81, C83-C84). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for challenge to single-mechanism theories. Peer review R9 addresses broader summary conclusions including some overlapping claims. Both rate as SUPPORTED with high praise for study impact.

Minimal overlap on connections to prior literature (C64, C66-C68). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for appropriate citations and cross-modal comparisons. Peer review R5 includes C68 in discussion of VIP functional interpretation rated as UNCERTAIN. Different evaluation scopes.

Minimal overlap on literature review claims (C85-C91). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for accurate summary of prior work. Peer review R9 includes some related claims (C89-C90) in broader summary evaluation. Both affirm these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates hypothesis C15 about adaptation as explanation for local violations, rating as SUPPORTED as testable hypothesis subsequently evaluated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific hypothesis formulation.

Minimal overlap on transition-probability-based predictions (C54). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on long inter-sequence interval experiments. Peer review R9 includes C54 in broader summary conclusions. Both affirm this finding.
